summary: PROMPT 20 (parcial) — Routal real adapter validated end-to-end. 9/9 unit tests pass + 8/8 NEW live ingress tests pass against the real Routal API at https://api.routal.com. Real tracking_id 16lfgtGFKg2XxT7B confirmed completed→delivered (terminal, confidence=100). 10 real plans returned from project 636aaed54235630d2258fa6d. Frontend /admin/cae/routal renders all 4 health KPIs (api_key/project_id/configured/pingable=200 OK), top-10 real plans table, and track form with raw payload (lat/lng/address/phone/email). RBAC blocks agent (403) on all 3 admin/cae/routal endpoints. cae_status_catalog (collection: carrier_status_catalog) has all 4 routal codes seeded alongside 5 anchor mock carriers (99min, dhl, estafeta, fedex, paqex).
critical_code_review_comments: RoutalAdapter: NATIVE_CODES (4 codes) match the spec exactly: pending→in_transit, incomplete→exception(failed,requires_action), completed→delivered(terminal), canceled→cancelled(terminal). Confidence values 95/92/100/100 are reasonable.

RoutalAdapter._search_stop_by_external_id: uses POST /v2/stops/search with predicate {field: external_id, op: eq} — correct; supports both list and {docs:[...]} response shapes. Returns None on non-200 (and logs) instead of raising — good defensive style.

RoutalAdapter.get_raw_status: when stop not found, returns RawCarrierEvent with raw_code='unknown' and found=False so the normalizer creates an entry in cae_unmapped_codes — clean fallback that keeps the ticket in seguimiento rather than blowing up.
RoutalAdapter._require_creds: raises VALIDATION_FAILED (not generic exception) so the API surfaces a 400-class error — correct domain error.
Adapter registration in anchor_stubs.py uses lazy import (_register_routal) to avoid breaking imports if httpx is missing in unrelated environments — sensible.

admin_routal.py: RBAC via require_min_role('admin') applied at router level via Depends — verified agent receives 403 on health/plans/track. tenant_id read from request.state.user passed to StatusNormalizer (multi-tenant correct).
admin_routal.py /plans: projects only safe public fields (id, label, status, total_stops, completed_stops, pending_stops, execution_date) — no leakage of private_key/internal IDs.
admin_routal.py /track: returns both raw and normalized payloads — useful for debugging/visualization. event_at serialized to isoformat string.

Frontend AdminRoutal.jsx: all required testids present (routal-health-card, routal-reload, routal-track-card, routal-track-input, routal-track-submit, routal-track-result, routal-plans-card, routal-plan-{id}). State machine handles loading/error/result correctly.
Frontend: Health card shows ALL 4 KPIs in a single 4-col grid (api_key/project/configured/pingable) — matches spec.
Frontend: Plans table renders 10 rows with #/Plan/Estado/Stops/Pendientes/Completados/Ejecución columns; pendientes vs completados color-coded (status-active/status-resolved) — clean viz.

Minor: routal.py._stop_to_event uses datetime.fromisoformat with Z→+00:00 swap — works for Routal's ISO-Z timestamps but bare; if Routal ever sends non-Z offsets it will still parse correctly since Python 3.11+ fromisoformat is lenient.

Minor: admin_routal.py imports RESEND_API_KEY from core.config purely as a side-effect to ensure env loaded — works but a more explicit `from dotenv import load_dotenv; load_dotenv()` at app boot would be clearer (this is presumably done in core.config already).

Minor: AdminRoutal.jsx Promise.all swallows /plans error with an empty list fallback (.catch) but health failure isn't caught — if /health 500s the entire page would stay in 'Cargando…' state. Consider a try/catch per-call to surface partial state.
Minor: RoutalAdapter.send_instruction is implemented but not wired into any callable endpoint yet — fine for this iteration, will be needed when the cancel-from-MyExcellence flow is built.
